title: Proof Strategy and Historical Context
content: Introduces the proof strategy for Kakutani's fixed point theorem from Brouwer's via approximate selections (Cellina 1969). The approach avoids simplicial approximation by using partitions of unity to construct continuous $\varepsilon$-approximate selections of the upper hemicontinuous correspondence, then applying Brouwer to each selection and extracting a limit via compactness. This file factors the proof into three independent axioms, isolating the exact infrastructure gaps in Mathlib.
mathContext: Kakutani's FPT (1941): if $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is nonempty, compact, convex, and $F: S \to 2^S$ is upper hemicontinuous with nonempty closed convex values, then $\exists x \in S: x \in F(x)$.

title: Set-Valued Maps and Upper Hemicontinuity
content: Defines the core abstractions: `SetValuedMap X Y` as a function $X \to \mathcal{P}(Y)$ (a correspondence), `IsFixedPoint F x` as $x \in F(x)$, and `IsUpperHemicontinuous F` requiring $\{x : F(x) \subseteq V\}$ is open for every open $V$. UHC is the standard continuity notion for set-valued maps in mathematical economics and game theory, weaker than lower hemicontinuity but sufficient for fixed point theorems when combined with convexity.
mathContext: Upper hemicontinuity: $F: X \to 2^Y$ is UHC if for every open $V \supseteq F(x_0)$, there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$ with $F(x) \subseteq V$ for all $x \in U$. Equivalently, the upper inverse $F^+(V) = \{x : F(x) \subseteq V\}$ is open for every open $V$. For single-valued maps, UHC coincides with ordinary continuity.

title: Brouwer's Fixed Point Theorem (Axiom 1)
content: Axiomatizes Brouwer's FPT for nonempty compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$: every continuous self-map has a fixed point. Mathlib proves this for closed balls via degree theory, but the general compact convex case requires homeomorphism to a ball (via the convex body theorem or direct retraction arguments). This is the topological pillar of the Kakutani proof.
mathContext: Brouwer's FPT: $f: S \to S$ continuous, $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ nonempty compact convex $\Rightarrow \exists x \in S: f(x) = x$. Equivalently: the identity on $S$ is not homotopic to a constant in $S \setminus \{x\}$ for any $x$. The theorem follows from the non-retractability of the ball onto its boundary.

title: Approximate Selections via Partition of Unity (Axiom 2)
content: Defines `IsApproxSelection F f ε` ($\forall x, \exists y \in F(x): d(f(x), y) < \varepsilon$) and axiomatizes existence of continuous $\varepsilon$-selections for UHC maps with convex values. The proof sketch in the docstring outlines the construction: cover $S$ by UHC neighborhoods, extract finite subcover by compactness, take subordinate partition of unity $\{\phi_i\}$, define $f(x) = \sum \phi_i(x) y_{x_i}$. Convexity of $S$ ensures $f(x) \in S$, and the UHC condition gives $d(f(x), F(x)) < \varepsilon$.
mathContext: Cellina's approximate selection theorem (1969): if $F: S \to 2^S$ is UHC with nonempty convex values and $S$ is compact, then for any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists continuous $f_\varepsilon: S \to S$ with $d(f_\varepsilon(x), F(x)) < \varepsilon$. The construction uses $f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^k \phi_i(x) \cdot y_i$ where $\{\phi_i\}$ is a partition of unity subordinate to the UHC cover and $y_i \in F(x_i)$.

title: Sequential Compactness (Axiom 3)
content: Axiomatizes that compact metric spaces are sequentially compact: every sequence in a compact set $S$ has a subsequence converging to a point in $S$. This is the analytical pillar providing the convergent subsequence $x_{k_j} \to x^*$ from the sequence of approximate fixed points. In metrizable spaces, sequential compactness is equivalent to compactness; Mathlib partially supports this but the specific subtype formulation is axiomatized here.
mathContext: Sequential compactness: $S$ compact in a metric space $\Rightarrow$ for every sequence $(x_n) \subseteq S$, there exist $a \in S$ and a strictly increasing $\phi: \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $x_{\phi(n)} \to a$. The Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem is the $\mathbb{R}^n$ special case.

title: Kakutani from Brouwer: The Combination Argument
content: The main theorem: combining all three axioms to prove Kakutani's FPT. For each $k \ge 1$: (1) apply Axiom 2 with $\varepsilon = 1/k$ to get continuous $f_k$; (2) apply Axiom 1 (Brouwer) to get $f_k(x_k) = x_k$; (3) apply Axiom 3 to extract $x_{k_j} \to x^*$; (4) use UHC and closedness to show $x^* \in F(x^*)$. Step 4 works because $d(x_k, F(x_k)) < 1/k \to 0$, so the limit point must belong to $F(x^*)$ by upper hemicontinuity (the graph of $F$ is closed in the appropriate sense).
mathContext: The contradiction in step 4: if $x^* \notin F(x^*)$ with $F(x^*)$ closed, then $\delta = d(x^*, F(x^*)) > 0$. By UHC, eventually $F(x_{k_j}) \subseteq B(F(x^*), \delta/2)$. But $d(x_{k_j}, F(x_{k_j})) < 1/k_j \to 0$, so $d(x_{k_j}, B(F(x^*), \delta/2)) \to 0$, giving $d(x^*, F(x^*)) \le \delta/2 < \delta$.

title: Approximate Fixed Points Imply True Fixed Points
content: The structural lemma `approx_fixedpoint_implies_fixedpoint`: if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists an $\varepsilon$-approximate fixed point in $S$ (a point $x$ with $d(x, F(x)) < \varepsilon$), then a true fixed point exists. This abstracts the limit argument from the main proof, making it reusable. The proof uses compactness to extract a limit and upper hemicontinuity to close the gap, mirroring step 4 of the Kakutani proof.
mathContext: The lemma captures the principle: $\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists x_\varepsilon \in S, \exists y_\varepsilon \in F(x_\varepsilon): d(x_\varepsilon, y_\varepsilon) < \varepsilon \;\Rightarrow\; \exists x^* \in S: x^* \in F(x^*)$. This is a set-valued analogue of the fact that a continuous function achieving $|f(x) - x| < \varepsilon$ for all $\varepsilon > 0$ has a fixed point.
